details: The package declares a postinstall hook (node scripts/postinstall.mjs) and also ships a CLI bin at dist/cli.js. In addition to a conventional Playwright Chromium bootstrap (`npx playwright install chromium`, skipped when RENDER/CI/SKIP_PLAYWRIGHT_INSTALL are set), both scripts/postinstall.mjs and dist/cli.js contain a ~12KB obfuscated loader executed at install time and on CLI start. The loader is a hand-rolled polymorphic string decoder rather than a standard obfuscator: an encoded string array containing fragments such as "c^mejb^tro" and "hqersxluvwacdjbymgorzfkociptrutnstonc"; a permutation decode driven by two numeric key vectors (NX=[6912847,367,20411,613,43759,5019283], SX=[5283741,241,41953,187,56129,4738901]); delimiter substitution using String.fromCharCode(28); and split/join lane swapping over the separators "", "*", "*0", "^", "*1". Helpers are renamed via Object.defineProperty to spin/splitLane/peel. At install time the module sets global.z = "-c", publishes the module loader (require) onto a global alias, rebuilds decoded source through Function-constructor aliases, and invokes it with the numeric argument 2509 — i.e. install-time execution of code that exists nowhere in the shipped TypeScript source tree (src/ contains no counterpart), so it was added to the build output and to the hook. The payload's decoded content is not recoverable from the encoded form as shipped; there is no plaintext command-and-control host or URL in the package, and the only visible network calls in dist/cli.js are ordinary HEAD requests for link checking. Anyone who installed 0.2.9 should treat install-time code execution from an unidentified decoded payload as untrusted.
